newsitem.title: GERMANY: Duisenberg wants spring '98 euro fx rate fix-paper.
newsitem.headline: Duisenberg wants spring '98 euro fx rate fix-paper.

text.p: Wim Duisenberg, the future head of the European Monetary Institute (EMI), is in favour of setting euro currency conversion rates in the spring of 1998, German business daily Handelsblatt said on Sunday.

As a basis for the conversion rates, the central parity rates of Europe's Exchange Rate Mechanism (ERM) could be used, the newspaper reported Duisenberg, who is currently the Dutch central bank governor, as saying.

This would not rule out the possibility that financial markets would test the strength of those levels, he added, but fixing the conversions early was safer than leaving the issue open for the seven or eight months between the decision on EMU particpants and the launch of the euro.
A summary of the Handelsblatt report, which is scheduled for publication on Monday, was released ahead of time.

Duisenberg, who is due to take over from the current EMI president Alexandre Lamfalussy on July 1, also said it was unlikely to be possible for individual EMU first round members to secure a competitive advantage by depreciating their currencies before the start of the euro in January 1999.
"In the light of cooperation between countries, that could not be pushed through," he said, adding that such action would also harm stability efforts.
